question: How Do I Duplicate an Existing Product to Use as a Template?
metaDescription: Built into WooCommerce core via the "Duplicate" row action on the Products list — copies everything except the SKU, which must stay unique.
shortAnswer: This is a built-in feature, not something needing a plugin — hovering over a product in the Products admin list reveals a "Duplicate" quick action, which creates a full copy of that product (as a draft) including its description, images, attributes, and settings, ready to be adjusted and published as a new listing. The SKU is deliberately left blank on the copy, since SKUs must be unique.

image.alt: A product being duplicated as a draft copy through a built-in quick action, ready to be customized and published as a new listing

bodyHtml:
How to Duplicate a Product

On the Products admin list, hovering over any product reveals row actions including "Duplicate" alongside Edit and Trash — clicking it immediately creates a new draft product with (almost) everything copied from the original, ready to open and adjust before publishing.

What Carries Over and What Doesn't

  • Description, short description, images, attributes, categories, and most settings all copy over directly, making this genuinely useful as a starting template for a similar new product.
  • The SKU is intentionally left blank on the duplicate, since SKUs must be unique and copying it directly would create a conflict — a new SKU needs to be manually assigned.
  • Reviews and sales/order history don't carry over, since the duplicate is a genuinely new, separate product with no history of its own.
  • The new product is created as a Draft, not automatically published, giving a chance to review and adjust everything (title, price, images, SKU) before it goes live.

Using This Feature Well

  1. Use Duplicate as a starting point for a new product genuinely similar to an existing one, saving setup time.
  2. Always assign a new, unique SKU to the duplicate before publishing.
  3. Review every field carefully before publishing, since it's easy to overlook something that should differ from the original (a unique description detail, a different price).
